summary.headline: Muthoot Microfin Q2 FY27: record Rs 2,900 cr disbursement, PAT Rs 110.8 cr standalone, average cost of borrowing cut to 9.93%.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly disbursement of Rs 2,900 crore (up 28% YoY), AUM of Rs 15,323 crore (up 22% YoY), and standalone PAT of Rs 110.8 crore (about Rs 111 crore). Credit cost was 2.6%, within the 2.5-3% guided range, and GNPA improved 32 bps QoQ to about 3.38%. Average cost of borrowing fell from 10.13% to 9.93%, the first time below 10% in company history. Management flagged the El Nino-linked drought in Maharashtra and Karnataka as a watch item, with about 3.6% of on-book portfolio (around Rs 550 crore) exposed and most of it covered by NATCAT insurance. FY27 guidance was reaffirmed.

financial_highlights.metric: Liquidity on balance sheet / unavailed sanctions
financial_highlights.value: Rs 1,835 crore / Rs 4,442 crore (corrected in errata)

segments.name: JLG (group loans)
segments.commentary: Share of portfolio fell to 69% from 83% at end-March FY27, ahead of the 70:30 full-year target. Group loans in Karnataka are 0.49% of on-book portfolio.

segments.name: Individual loans (Muthoot small and growing business)
segments.commentary: Portfolio at Rs 4,164 crore, 27% of AUM, with 90+ dpd at 0.02%. About 2.7 lakh of 32 lakh customers graduated from JLG at 700+ credit score.

segments.name: Gold loans (co-lending with Muthoot Fincorp)
segments.commentary: Rs 453 crore gold loans disbursed in Q2. Management bought back a Rs 200 crore referral-originated gold loan assignment from Muthoot Fincorp; yield about 12-12.5% effective (1.5% upfront fee plus about 9.8% margin, around 5-month tenure).

segments.name: Micro LAP
segments.commentary: AUM crossed Rs 100 crore in October; about 18 months seasoning with near-zero delinquency.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance fully intact: AUM growth about 20% (earlier guided 18-20%, revised to 20%).
Credit cost expected to come in better than the 2.5-3% guidance range.
NIM expected at the upper end of guidance, with management saying it will exceed it.
ROA expected at the upper end; management cited 3.3% as the upper bracket and 18% ROE, and expects to beat both.
FY27 PAT guidance of Rs 425-450 crore; H1 PAT Rs 192 crore, with management expecting Q3 and Q4 to be stronger.
Long-term target of Rs 30,000 crore AUM by 2030 reaffirmed; growth possible without fresh capital.
Targets: AUM per branch Rs 12-13 crore (currently Rs 9.1 crore) and OPEX/AUM 5.5-5.75% (currently 6.1% of GLP); digital collection 75% (currently 47%) reached earlier than 2030.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 1,675; expansion focus on Assam, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, with Jammu and Kashmir entry planned soon. No new infrastructure added for individual loans (run from existing branches) or gold loans (served through Muthoot Fincorp branches).
AUM per branch Rs 9.1 crore vs Rs 7.3 crore earlier; AUM per loan officer about Rs 1.8 crore (errata; transcript said 1.8 million).
Branch profitability module identified 80 under-performing branches for merger, rationalisation or redeployment.
Customer app used by 2.2 million customers; Suvidha digital loan (disbursed within 30 minutes, E-NACH based) with Rs 1.5 crore disbursed so far.
demand_pricing: Disbursement momentum expected to continue into a seasonally stronger H2 and festive season.

Drought exposure: 34 affected districts across Maharashtra (3.1% of on-book) and Karnataka (0.49%); about 3.6% of portfolio, around Rs 550 crore, with 81-85% covered by NATCAT insurance. Less than 2% of portfolio directly rain-dependent. Management plans calibrated disbursement, tilting to secured products in affected districts.
Assam exposure below Rs 100 crore (100% NATCAT covered); Bihar about Rs 1,000 crore, with floods partly covered by NATCAT and drought not affecting collections.

Cost of funds pressure: management acknowledged a 25 bps rate hike, expects pass-through over time and further hikes, but says it can negotiate given Rs 1,835 crore liquidity and about Rs 4,442 crore unavailed sanctions.
PTC (securitisation) funding at about 8% average from private and foreign banks; Rs 250 crore NCD at 9.25%; ECB first draw-down possibly in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is exposure to other drought-hit states, and will disbursement slow there?
qa_highlights.answer: Coverage in 21 states; no trend seen outside Maharashtra and Karnataka. About 85% of portfolio has NATCAT cover. Disbursement is continuing (up about 27%), with calibrated lending and a secured-product tilt in affected districts.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan asset quality given industry stress in short-tenure gold lending?
qa_highlights.answer: No challenges seen. Management cites conservative LTV, income-based underwriting and eligibility-based funding.

qa_highlights.question: CGFMU status and IRDAI draft regulation impact?
qa_highlights.answer: CGFMU applied for, awaiting budget allocation, with the company first in the queue. IRDAI draft has been commented on; insurance revenue is under 5% of total revenue and is a pass-through model, so no material impact expected.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for cost of funds with rising rates?
qa_highlights.answer: A 25 bps hike has occurred and pass-through will occur over time. Management expects further hikes but says it can negotiate, citing liquidity, longer-tenure products, NCDs, ECB sanctions and PTC pricing near 8%.

qa_highlights.question: Collection trends in Maharashtra and the SRO/RBI response?
qa_highlights.answer: Maharashtra X-bucket collection at about 98%, stable; Karnataka at 100%. More than 60% of first-time defaulters said they will keep paying. SROs have issued guidance on empathetic collection and media clarification.

qa_highlights.question: Why buy back Rs 200 crore of gold loan assignments from Muthoot Fincorp?
qa_highlights.answer: Loans originated under the referral model (1.5% upfront fee) are being brought onto the company's books because the customers are its own. Yield is about 12-12.5% effective on a roughly 5-month tenure.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the ECL release, and what is the credit cost without it?
qa_highlights.answer: The release reflects portfolio improvement in the ECL model. Credit cost stays around 2.6%. Coverage is about 69.6-69.9%, and a Rs 24 crore contingency buffer is held for drought-like risks.

risks_watch: Drought in Maharashtra and Karnataka (around Rs 550 crore, 34 districts) could affect collections beyond the current 98-99% levels, though NATCAT cover is 81-85%.
Rising rate environment: management expects further hikes, so cost of borrowing could move above 9.93%.
ECL release this quarter may reverse if portfolio conditions weaken; buffer is Rs 24 crore. Provision coverage of about 70% is to be held.
Regulatory items: IRDAI draft insurance regulation on NATCAT pass-through model; CGFMU budget allocation still pending; SRO and RBI scrutiny of collection practices.
Growing non-JLG mix (31% of AUM) and individual loans (27%) are relatively new and seasoned only about 2 years; early-stage performance still to be proven. Gold lending is growing alongside.
Watch H2 profit delivery: H1 PAT Rs 192 crore against Rs 425-450 crore full-year guidance; ROA 3% vs guided upper bracket of 3.3%.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, funding and asset quality, repeating that guidance will be met or beaten. Cautious on the drought and macro backdrop, with answers stressing limited exposure and NATCAT cover. Some answers were loose on figures, including several errata in the transcript.
key_quotes: We recorded our highest ever quarterly dis bursal of Rs. 2,900 crores.
We have reached there in quarter 2 itself. Our average cost of borrowing has come down from 10.13% to 9.93%.
So, liquidity is not a constraint, and we have good room to negotiate for better rates.
The exposure for us is very limited. It is around 3.6% of our portfolio is in these two states, which is on -book portfolio, about Rs. 550 crores.
We will definitely achieve the guidance and may go beyond.

adds.what: Branch network expansion (Assam, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana; Jammu and Kashmir entry planned soon); branch count 1,675, no specific new branch numbers given

growth.why: Management reaffirmed about 20% AUM growth for FY27 (revised up from 18-20%), with Q2 disbursement up 28% YoY to Rs 2,900 crore and AUM up 22%, backed by a 1,675-branch network, a stated AUM-per-branch target of Rs 12-13 crore versus Rs 9.1 crore today, and FY27 PAT guidance of Rs 425-450 crore against H1 PAT of Rs 192 crore; the brief gives no new capacity numbers, so backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM at 12.5% (up from 12.0%) and management expects the upper end of 12.3-12.5% guidance and says it will exceed it, though a 25 bps rate hike is being passed through over time and cost of borrowing is 9.93%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Branch network at 1,675 with expansion into Assam, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and a planned Jammu and Kashmir entry, but no new branch counts or capex were given and AUM per branch is 9.1 crore against a 12-13 crore target, so growth is mostly from existing branches.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 disbursement up 28% YoY to Rs 2,900 crore, AUM up 22% to Rs 15,323 crore, and FY27 AUM growth of about 20% reaffirmed, with H2 and festive season seasonally stronger, offset by calibrated lending in drought districts.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex was discussed; the company runs individual loans from existing branches and gold loans through Muthoot Fincorp branches, and it is targeting higher AUM per branch rather than adding capacity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says it expects to beat ROA (3.3% upper bracket), ROE (18%), and NIM guidance, and expects credit cost below the 2.5-3% range, with H1 PAT of Rs 192 crore against FY27 PAT guidance of Rs 425-450 crore and Q3/Q4 expected to be stronger.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Drought exposure of about Rs 550 crore (3.6% of on-book, 81-85% NATCAT covered), further rate hikes that could push cost of borrowing above 9.93%, and an ECL release that may reverse, against an H2 PAT need of about Rs 233-258 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Micro LAP (AUM above Rs 100 crore, about 18 months seasoned), Suvidha digital loan (Rs 1.5 crore disbursed so far) and gold loan co-lending are already live, but no new product launch dates were given.

rows.label: Cost of funds pass-through and rate-hike negotiation
rows.why: A 25 bps hike has occurred and management expects pass-through and further hikes, but says it can negotiate with Rs 1,835 crore liquidity and Rs 4,442 crore unavailed sanctions; PTC funding is about 8%.

rows.label: Branch rationalisation and digital collections
rows.why: 80 under-performing branches identified for merger, rationalisation or redeployment; OPEX/AUM at 6.1% against a 5.5-5.75% target, and digital collection at 47% against a 75% target.

rows.label: Growth without fresh capital; ECB first draw-down
rows.why: Management says growth to Rs 30,000 crore AUM by 2030 is possible without fresh capital, with capital adequacy at 25.5% and an ECB first draw-down possibly in Q3.
